title: When the Typewriter Breaks
premise: In the city of Vellmarin, 1848, Odile Ravensworth works in her father's print shop, cutting type and believing revolutions are things that happen in capitals, to strangers. When a census taker discovers a hidden ledger of names — dissidents marked for arrest — hidden inside a broken typewriter-like composing machine left by her late mother, Odile realizes her mother was not who she claimed to be. With the census taker, Anselm, now compromised by what he has seen, they must carry the ledger across the city through three military checkpoints before dawn raids destroy every name within it. Odile reaches the last checkpoint wounded but succeeds, delivering the ledger to the printers' guild; in the aftermath she learns her mother's true name is carved into its final page, and she chooses to sign her own beside it.
about_author: Rosalind Ishikawa is a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century printing equipment before turning to fiction. She writes historical novels about the people history forgets — the hands that set the type, not the names on the page.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A day in the Ravensworth print shop: sorting type, mending the temperamental composing machine her mother left behind, dodging her father's melancholy. Establishes her conviction that history happens elsewhere. Emotional beat: quiet restlessness beneath routine.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. The annual census visit goes wrong when Anselm, cataloging household goods for the state, notices the strange machine and asks whose work it was. Odile's evasive answer unsettles them both. Emotional beat: first crack in the ordinary world.

chapters.title: What the Machine Kept
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Cleaning the machine after a jam, she finds a false panel and the hidden ledger — pages of names, coded trades, meeting places. Her mother's handwriting. Emotional beat: vertigo of discovering a stranger where a parent should be.

chapters.title: The Man Who Counts
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. Haunted by the ledger glimpse, Anselm returns off-duty and confesses he reported the machine's serial number as required by law. The registry will flag it within days. Emotional beat: guilt and reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Names Are Not Ink
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She deciphers entries: neighbors, the baker's son, a schoolmistress — all marked. Realizing arrests are imminent, she and Anselm argue over whether to burn it or save it. Emotional beat: fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Her Mother's Hand
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Studying the ledger's codes, she recognizes typeface habits only a cutter would know — her mother built this cipher herself. Flashbacks to childhood lessons disguised as games. Emotional beat: grief braided with pride.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They map the route to the printers' guild across the river: the market gate, the bridge, the customs house. Each demands papers and searches carts. Emotional beat: the plan taking shape, terror at its margins.

chapters.title: The Baker's Son
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. One listed name, Lucien, comes to the shop asking if his father's name is 'in something.' Odile lies badly. He guesses, and insists on helping. Emotional beat: the ledger stops being abstract — it has a face.

chapters.title: Forging Papers
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. Using his census authority, Anselm alters travel permits, knowing discovery means prison. A superior grows suspicious of his extra ink requisitions. Emotional bet: sacrifice made concrete, no way back.

chapters.title: First Checkpoint: The Market Gate
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The ledger sewn into a bolt of linen, Odile passes the gate by trading on her shopkeeper's respectability — until a guard asks her mother's maiden name. She answers with a name she invents. Emotional beat: first lie told in her mother's voice.

chapters.title: Raids at Dawn
chapters.summary: Lucien's POV. Soldiers arrest the schoolmistress down the street; Lucien watches from the bakery and realizes time has collapsed. He warns Odile via chalk mark on the shop door. Emotional beat: dread accelerating, the city turning hostile.

chapters.title: The Father Who Knew
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Her father reveals he always suspected his wife's double life and chose silence to protect Odile. He gives her his own escape papers instead of hers. Emotional beat: inheritance reframed — love passed down as risk.

chapters.title: Second Checkpoint: The Bridge
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. Anselm carries the ledger this time, posing as transporting census records. His suspicious superior appears at the bridge; Anselm bluffs with genuine forms, sweating through the search. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by exposure.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Guildhall
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The printers' guild contact they trusted turns out to be informing for reward money. They barely escape; the safe route is burned. Emotional beat: trust shattered, stakes doubled.

chapters.title: The Long Way Round
chapters.summary: Lucien's POV. Lucien offers the smugglers' tunnels under the tanneries he knows from boyhood. The three move by night through dark and reek, learning each other's fears. Emotional beat: unlikely fellowship forged underground.

chapters.title: What Anselm Carries
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. In the tunnels, Anselm admits he once erased a family from the census to save them — and one name slipped through anyway. The ledger is his penance. Emotional beat: confession as absolution sought, not granted.

chapters.title: Third Checkpoint: The Customs House
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The final barrier: full body search, ledgers opened, Odile's forged papers questioned by an officer who knew her mother. She claims her invented maiden name again — and the officer hesitates, recognizing something true in her face. Emotional beat: identity as performance and truth at once.

chapters.title: Dawn Raids, Second Night
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. As they wait out curfew before delivery, soldiers raid the print shop; her father burns the decoy records and is taken for questioning. Emotional beat: cost made real; the climax's engine ignites.

chapters.title: The Last Hundred Yards
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At dawn, carrying the ledger openly under a guild banner Lucien procured, Odile walks past the checkpoint crowd as arrests begin around her. A soldier grabs her arm; Anselm creates a diversion and is seized. Emotional beat: courage stripped of romance — just walking forward.

chapters.title: Delivered
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She reaches the guild press room; the ledger goes to the typesetters even as gunfire sounds outside. Names begin printing on broadsheets distributed through the streets. Emotional beat: catharsis — memory made public, ink outrunning soldiers.

chapters.title: After the Revolution Wakes
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV, released in the chaos. Vellmarin changes hands without battle as the printed names turn public opinion. Anselm finds Odile amid celebration; both understand they were never bystanders. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning, tenderness in wreckage.

chapters.title: Two Names on One Page
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Rebuilding the shop, Odile finds the ledger's final page: her mother's true name, signed like a compositor signs a finished plate. Odile cuts new type and adds her own signature beneath it. Emotional beat: resolution — inheritance accepted, identity chosen.
